text:
claire_support: heads up — Support ticket #4521 just escalated, multiple customers seeing 5xx and timeouts against /v1/generate since ~08:40 UTC. Error spike correlates with the canary rolled at 08:36.

dave_sre: seeing it on SRE dashboards: 5xx rate across us-west increased from 0.4% to 12% in ~3 min, p95 latency also jumped. traces show gateway 502 and 504 responses.

ben_oncall: any recent config flips?

alice_dev: I pushed a canary at 08:36 that changed `routing.pinning` to `true` for the experiment group to try to reduce KV cache misses. It should only affect 5% of traffic.

claire_support: customers report partial failures — some requests succeed, others return `502 Gateway Error: shard unavailable` or timeouts. Examples in the ticket: request_id=rx-8a12, rx-8a13, rx-8a20.

dave_sre: grabbing a few traces. looks like requests routed to model-variant v2b sometimes hit an uninitialized worker which returns 502 quickly, other times it times out waiting for initialization (504).

infra-bot: alert: canary-deploy 2026-03-17T08:36:22 UTC — feature: routing.pinning=true — traffic 5%

ben_oncall: ok if the canary only targeted 5% but errors are cascading, we should pause/rollback the canary. Who can flip it?

alice_dev: i can flip the flag, but need coordination with routing controller team — flipping quickly may cause transient reroutes.

emma_prod: ticket has 3 paying customers impacted (mid-market) complaining about request billing spikes because of retries. We should proactively credit them; need to capture affected request_ids.

claire_support: capturing request_ids now, will add to the ticket. Suggest rollback asap and mitigation to disable pinning globally until we root cause.

dave_sre: agree. Ben, can you run the rollback playbook?

ben_oncall: starting rollback runbook step 1: set canary traffic to 0%. Running `curl -X POST https://orch.internal/api/v1/flags/routing.pinning/traffic -d '{"percent":0}'`

alice_dev: hold on — if we set percent=0 that will re-route to default which may be on overloaded workers. Can we instead set `routing.pinning=false` for the canary config? that's quicker.

ben_oncall: ok switching to direct flag toggle. Running:
```
POST /api/v1/flags/routing.pinning
{ "value": false, "scope": "canary-2026-03-17" }
```

infra-bot: config-change accepted by orchestrator — ID cfg-8891.

deploy-bot: canary update: routing.pinning=false applied to canary-2026-03-17 at 08:47:02 UTC.

claire_support: customer reports initial improvement, but still seeing intermittent 5xxs for past 6 minutes.

dave_sre: rolling back canary isn't instant for some in-flight requests. Also we observed route table convergence delays. Kicking a manual route refresh to all edge routers now.

ben_oncall: route refresh command issued: `orchctl refresh-routes --all-regions` — watching logs.

alice_dev: i'm running a small script to identify workers that never finished initialization during canary. snippet:
```bash
for id in $(cat failed_workers.txt); do ssh infra@$id 'systemctl status inference-worker || journalctl -u inference-worker -n 200'; done
```

emma_prod: for billing credits, can we generate a CSV of impacted request_ids + customer_id? i'll prep the credit note template.

claire_support: added request_ids to ticket and attached logs. will draft customer outreach: apology + credit + ETA for postmortem.

dave_sre: initial root cause hypothesis: enabling `routing.pinning` caused some requests to be pinned to a subset of workers that were in scale-up state (zero-warmed containers for model v2b). Our autoscaler didn't pre-warm because pinned routing bypasses prefetch heuristic. When traffic pinned to those workers, they either returned shard-unavailable (502) or timed out (504) waiting for init.

alice_dev: we tested pre-warming in staging but didn't replicate the exact shard allocation pattern. shipping a patch to detect zero-warmed workers and fallback to non-pinned routing when worker-init exceed 300ms. patch in PR #982.

ben_oncall: recommend immediate mitigations: 1) ensure canary flag off (done), 2) add a short-circuit that routes pinned requests to fallback pool if worker not ready, 3) proactively credit impacted customers.

emma_prod: agreed. I'll coordinate credits with finance and the account teams — need CSV within 30 min.

claire_support: customers updated and SLA credit offers in flight. posting status update to status.redwood.ai.

deploy-bot: post to status: incident-1777777000 — partial outage for hosted inference in us-west, mitigation underway.

dave_sre: creating incident channel and scheduling a 15-min triage huddle at 09:10 UTC.

alice_dev: merging hotfix that adds fallback checks to routing controller. will deploy to canary=0.5% then monitor.

ben_oncall: after change, monitor p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate, and initialization errors. set an automated rollback if 5xx > 1% for 3 consecutive minutes.

claire_support: keep customer comms updated. I'll collect follow-ups for the postmortem (test coverage gap, canary guardrails, autoscaler pre-warm assumptions, billing protections).

dave_sre: noted. tagging for postmortem: alice_dev (author), ben_oncall (rollback), dave_sre (infrastructure), claire_support (customer impact), emma_prod (billing).

ben_oncall: monitoring shows 5xx dropping to baseline after route refresh ~08:55. continuing to watch for 10 more min.

claire_support: ticket owners confirmed customers received credits and initial message. closing escalation once metrics stable.

deploy-bot: canary patch deployed to 0.5% at 09:03 UTC — monitoring.

dave_sre: follow-up action items:
- add guardrail to disallow `routing.pinning=true` unless pre-warm signals confirm pool warm
- improve staging to simulate shard allocation
- add telemetry for pinned-request fallbacks
- run billing-impact report weekly for infra incidents

claire_support: agreed. creating postmortem doc and will assign owners. Thanks everyone :heart:
